US OCTOBER CPI REPORT TO OMIT ANNUAL INFLATION FIGURES The Bureau of Labor Statistics will exclude year-over-year headline and core CPI figures from Tuesday's October inflation report. Missing October 2025 price data from last year's government shutdown prevents reliable annual comparisons. Annual real earnings growth will also be unavailable. Monthly inflation figures will still be released. Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.3% MoM and core CPI to increase 0.2% MoM.

Nearly 40% intend to reduce investment, and 80% expect production to stagnate or decline. US 10-YEAR TREASURY AUCTION SEES WEAKER DEMAND AS YIELD TOPS 5% The US Treasury sold $42 billion in 10-year notes at a high yield of 5.02%, above the 5.010% when-issued yield before the auction. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.46 from 2.77 at the previous auction, signaling weaker investor demand. The auction tailed by 1 basis point, as investors demanded a higher yield to absorb the debt. Treasury yields are back above 5%, adding pressure to bonds, borrowing costs and equity valuations.
